messages:
alex_infra: Heads-up — eu-west1 is hitting a GPU capacity surge right now. A bunch of low-priority batch jobs queued and CA is not provisioning new GPU nodes due to quota errors.
priya: I see the spike on the dashboard. Any recent infra changes or quota sweeps? :eyes:
dani: Not that I know of. Only thing changed was the larger batch campaign from recommendations team this morning.
alex_infra: Here are the failing events from the autoscaler logs:
```
E0516 08:12:34 cluster_autoscaler.go:123] Failed to create instance: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project 12345 in region europe-west1., quotaExceeded
W0516 08:12:34 cluster_autoscaler.go:456] No nodes created for 5m due to resource constraints
```
jason_ops: Ouch. Cloud quota is the blocker, not K8s scheduling. We can either request quota increase (slow) or route some batch to fallback non-GPU pipelines.
priya: Is there any unused reserved capacity we can borrow from other regions (eu-central / west europe)? Cross-region cold spillover might add latency but keeps jobs moving.
alex_infra: We have some underutilized dedicated pools in europe-central but they're tainted for non-prod. We could temporary untaint or add a nodeAffinity fallback for low-priority jobs.
dani: Suggestion: add a nodeSelector on the batch job template for fallback pools: `nodeSelector: { "gpu-type": "none", "pool": "batch-fallback" }` and a label-based admission webhook to toggle during quota events.
priya: Before doing that, check the risk of spilling to non-GPU—jobs will need a CPU-only code path. Do they have that? I'll ping the recommendations team.
alex_infra: Quick mitigation I pushed: created a new node pool 'batch-spill-eu' with smaller GPU count per node and lower preemptible priority, and increased autoscaler max surge for that pool.
scheduler-bot: NOTE: autoscaler config updated for pool=batch-spill-eu: --max-total-unready-percentage=40 --max-node-provisioning-per-minute=3
jason_ops: Can you paste the kubectl get nodes output for that pool?
alex_infra: Sure:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=batch-spill-eu -o wide
NAME                          STATUS   ROLES    AGE  VERSION
gke-batch-spill-eu-1          Ready    <none>   5m   v1.26
gke-batch-spill-eu-2          Ready    <none>   3m   v1.26
```
priya: Good. Two nodes up already. But global quota still limits scaling above this level.
dani: Longer-term: we should add autoscaler logic to prefer spilling to non-GPU pools when regional GPU quota is low, and to automatically requeue without failing pods. Maybe a custom expander plugin?
alex_infra: Agreed. Proposed config change (quick patch):
```
--expander=priority
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--max-node-provisioning-per-minute=4
```
This lets CA favor lower-priority smaller nodes during bursts.
jason_ops: Also request a quota bump for europe-west1 GPUs, put a ticket to cloud support. I can do the ticket now.
priya: I'll coordinate with recommendations team to enable CPU fallback for their job runner; that buys us breathing room.
infra-bot: Incident created: GPU-capacity-surge-eu-west1 (ID: INC-20260516-23). Pager duty notified.
alex_infra: After spillover enabled, queue dropped from 370 -> 48 over 12 minutes. Monitoring watch for next 2 hours.
priya: Nice. Postmortem action items: 1) autoscaler spillover policy, 2) cross-region quota runbook, 3) job-level CPU fallback flag. I'll create a doc and assign owners.
jason_ops: Filed quota request + CC'ed infra-sre. Ticket ID: GQ-98732.
alex_infra: Thanks all. If we see another wave, we'll flip additional fallback labels and throttle batch submission rate on the producer side.
priya: Throttling rule added on recommendations producer: rate-limit=20/s for now.
alex_infra: Closing thread for now — will post updates in the INC when resolved. :white_check_mark:
